milestones.remaining: The 101-row partial-scope audit reconciles 433 components and audits 316 source paths, but is not proven to cover the full domain. Reconciliation against current source reduced stale code_incomplete classifications from 13 to 4: eight items already have callable bounded APIs and were reclassified as provider- or validation-dependent. Four code-scope gaps remain in wet-CO2 activity/ionic-strength coupling, competing multiphase kinetics and moving-boundary extensions, crevice fully coupled evolving flow/geometry and reactions, general nonproportional fatigue laws, automatic temporal pairing, alternative time reconstruction, and qualification; an explicit caller cycle-map plus calibrated FS/Miner API is now registered, and nonlinear/structurally coupled gasket behavior. Crevice now has a digest-pinned sequential cellwise recession-to-aperture remap within provider support, reconciles source wall areas, and emits RestrictedTransportRequest cell/face geometry fields for subsequent fixed-geometry solves; a fully coupled solver remains absent. Multiaxial fatigue now also evaluates exact finite-plane time factors conditional on an explicitly reviewed piecewise-linear tensor reconstruction. Wet-CO2 split transport now shares a digest-pinned caller activity callback between transport drift and single-solid projection, while a caller-defined fixed-gamma mass-action solver is now available; simultaneous multiphase and activity-feedback speciation remain absent. A continuous-plane Lipschitz upper bound for the supplied sampled cycle, signed time-varying flow/reversal callbacks, and caller-calibrated linear viscoelastic gasket histories now have bounded calculation APIs. Rare-event replicate/precision APIs are implemented; convergence, bias, and physical/model qualification remain validation work. This is source-scope review, not execution or scientific qualification. A separate coupled linear-viscoelastic gasket/elastic-bolt history API now solves closed-contact equilibrium at each declared knot using caller Prony data; contact opening and spatial flange behavior remain unsupported. A caller-defined aqueous mass-action API now solves a square single-liquid system in log-activity coordinates from explicit equilibrium reactions, fixed activity coefficients, linear analytical/charge constraints and caller initial guesses; it does not include phase changes or gamma iteration. Spatial linear-Prony gasket contact now has a caller-operator, knotwise unilateral contact API; nonlinear spatial viscoelastic response and within-interval contact transitions remain unsupported. A caller-tabulated, species-specific ln(activity coefficient) interpolation is now available inside finite ionic-strength support for coupling to the aqueous mass-action solver; the tables remain user-owned and require model-specific qualification. The closed-tensor fatigue work-life API now supports an explicit-derivative cubic-Hermite stress/strain path reconstruction with exact segment-work integration, in addition to piecewise-linear paths; this does not provide a universal nonproportional damage law. A caller nonlinear generalized-Maxwell gasket history is now coupled to spatial unilateral contact using the flange compliance operator and caller free-closure history at declared knots; no within-interval contact transition is inferred. 2026-10-30 update: competitive neutral pure-solid equilibrium now has a bounded Gibbs-potential extent API; automated speciation and precipitation kinetics remain absent. Steady variable-aperture laminar slit flow now supplies face velocities to the restricted-transport contract, but transient momentum and simultaneous flow/chemistry/recession coupling remain absent. 2026-10-30 update: pressure-sampled normal slit flow is now recalculated at each digest-bound aperture-history knot and both calculators are registered under crevice_chemistry; transient momentum and simultaneous coupling remain absent. A solver-matrix reduction now converts reviewed constrained translational stiffness to the gasket contact compliance operator; the mesh/FE solve and seal validation remain external. Time-indexed external flange stiffness matrices can now be reduced to an aligned contact-compliance operator history; the interval structural response remains provider-supplied. A caller-rate competing-solid ledger now applies declared signed precipitation/dissolution extents with inventory limits and elemental/charge closure; rate-law prediction, phase selection and activity-coupled kinetics remain absent. A fixed-geometry transport/competing-solid caller-rate interface now applies a per-cell phase ledger after each exact output-clock interval, preserves callback global time, and tracks separate transport/kinetic aqueous source balances; fully coupled activity/phase kinetics and moving geometry remain absent. A caller-reviewed maximum contact-time spacing now adds linearly interpolated gasket closure knots and sampled-state transition brackets bounded by that spacing; exact roots and multiple transitions inside one bracket remain unresolved. A caller-reviewed Davies ionic-strength fixed-point wrapper now couples the declared competing neutral-solid Gibbs equilibrium; automatic phase discovery, aqueous network generation, kinetic precipitation and concentrated-electrolyte models remain absent. A callback-based fixed-geometry operator split now composes cellwise competitive neutral-solid Davies equilibria with restricted transport and separate phase/transport inventory ledgers; simultaneous chemistry/transport coupling, phase kinetics and evolving geometry remain absent. The competitive-solid transport split was tightened to require the complete transport/phase species and charge inventory, add a physical-scope identity and projection record budget, and atomically commit each interval only after phase and aggregate/cell ledgers validate; failed later intervals preserve the completed prefix. A caller area-average scale-coverage law now supports constant saturation in closed form and explicitly reviewed piecewise-linear saturation with adaptive RK4 and attachment/detachment inventory closure. The synthetic input illustrates both forcing modes. A caller saturation-rate mapper now translates interval phase ratios through phase-specific power laws into the conservative multiphase ledger. Its transport interface can evaluate a caller callback on each post-transport right-knot aqueous/solid cell state and apply the derived rate after transport; this remains lagged operator splitting and does not compute saturation/speciation or solve simultaneous chemistry and transport. Adaptive aperture-change rejection and time-bisection are now available for the sequential crevice recession operator split, guarded by deterministic callback review and explicit budgets; fully coupled moving-boundary flow and chemistry are still absent. The crevice recession campaign now optionally computes a reviewed steady slit-flow field at the initial and accepted pressure/aperture knots and supplies each field to the following transport segment; it remains operator-split and excludes dynamic momentum. A stale gasket scope statement was corrected: time-varying flange compliance is linearly interpolated during replayed transition refinement, and bracket endpoint operator digests are now returned. The tabulated aqueous activity interface now offers optional reviewed shape-preserving PCHIP interpolation in log-gamma space on declared ionic-strength and temperature axes, without extrapolation; this is interpolation only and does not close electrolyte thermodynamics. A bounded, manually reviewed stoichiometric candidate enumerator for aqueous reactions is now registered; automatic reaction discovery and chemistry/phase selection remain explicitly absent. A bounded single-pure-salt Pitzer virial API now broadens the caller-parameterized aqueous activity methods without assigning individual-ion coefficients or introducing GPL dependencies. A SIT transport callback now applies the declared directional SIT expression at each restricted-transport mouth/cell and carries the parameter and Evidence lineage; simultaneous speciation-transport coupling and broader multiphase/moving-geometry chemistry remain incomplete. A SIT-to-saturation adapter now composes the caller-reviewed molality activity provider with the existing solid Ksp screen and competing-solid transport ledger; it retains the sequential operator split and does not close multiphase/moving-boundary coupling. Kinetic outputs retain the activity-provider lineage object and aggregate digest from the SIT-to-saturation composition callback. Competing-solid precipitation and dissolution coefficients can now optionally use caller activation energies relative to an explicit reference temperature, with a dedicated applicability review and effective-rate diagnostics; they remain empirical caller parameters requiring later validation. The caller phase-rate law now supports separate precipitation/dissolution Arrhenius activation energies only with a reference temperature, an explicit valid temperature interval, and an applicability review; result diagnostics retain effective coefficients and fail on range or numeric-support violations. Saturation-driven phase kinetics now accepts optional piecewise-constant interval temperatures (with the campaign temperature as fallback) and applies each value to Arrhenius laws and their explicit support gate. A new bounded caller-curve mapping supports a generic shear-plus-weighted-normal-strain parameter on finite sampled planes; it does not close general path-sensitive multiaxial material laws or their qualification. The generic caller-curve method now has a source-catalog derivation and synthetic builder example; material curve qualification and broad path-dependent law implementation remain open. The caller-calibrated gasket leakage table now has exact interval integration for its declared piecewise-linear pressure/bilinear-flux combination; the gasket joint scope remains incomplete in FE response generation, unresolved multiple contact transitions and sealing qualification. Gasket calibrated leakage interval totals now have axis-knot-split exact integration for linear pressure paths, with declared table-cell and subinterval budgets; the broader flange mechanics and sealing qualification gaps remain. The gasket leakage calculator now guards cumulative finite range, enforces total table-cell and integration-subinterval budgets, records a calibration-map digest, and uses binary-search axis bracketing for caller tables. Scale coverage attachment/detachment rates can now optionally use caller-provided Arrhenius scaling bounded by an explicit temperature applicability interval; rate parameters, independent validation and autonomous morphology remain open. The uniform single-phase scale thickness rate API now also supports separately caller-calibrated Arrhenius precipitation and dissolution rates inside explicit temperature support; experimental law qualification and automated scale chemistry remain incomplete. Caller single-phase scale thickness kinetics now supports constant or explicitly reviewed linear saturation endpoints with exact positive-part power integration across saturation and chronological precipitation/dissolution inventory limits; chemistry-derived saturation and rate laws, phase competition, morphology/adhesion, transport and qualification remain outside this API. Gasket leakage now has a deterministic exact pressure-interval rate envelope per node for the fixed bilinear calibration; probabilistic calibration uncertainty, cross-node correlations, FE generation, seal acceptance and qualification remain open. New code increments add local analytical sensitivity to fixed-gamma aqueous equilibrium, a caller-input crevice Nernst half-cell history, certified continuous-plane FS factor-to-life interval mapping, and an exact deterministic gasket leakage pressure-interval envelope. Each API remains conditional on explicit caller data and does not close broader qualification or physics gaps. The aqueous equilibrium Jacobian sensitivities now optionally propagate a caller-reviewed parameter covariance into first-order log-activity and concentration covariance; nonlinear/global uncertainty and covariance estimation remain open. The Nernst potential history now also composes with a caller-calibrated Butler–Volmer reaction at exact shared knots, returning digest-linked partial-current and species-flux history; no multi-reaction mixed-potential chemistry or total metal-loss closure is implied. Four new bounded adapters add curve-to-life, local crevice inventory, gasket threshold events, and exact-knot layered scale transport; they extend but do not complete their broad parent scopes. The newly added layered-scale exact-knot transport API also extends but does not close wet-CO2 scope. The CoQTEL typed row reader and finite scale reactant-inventory ledger are now registered, schema-exported and documented; neither closes its broader parent scope.
